about: County and city grant programs in Florida, entered by hand from each program's own page. grantmatch/local.py checks this file and turns each entry into a Florida program record. Change an entry only from the official page, and update its checked date.

programs.title: Children's Services Investment
programs.agency: Manatee County, Human Services Division, Children's Section
programs.objectives: Grants to agencies for programs that serve Manatee County children and families, paid from the county's dedicated children's services property tax. The Children's Services Advisory Board reviews applications and the Board of County Commissioners makes the final awards. Earlier cycles asked for programs serving children from before birth to age 17 who are at risk or economically disadvantaged; check the current guidance.
programs.who: Agencies serving Manatee County residents that have 501(c)(3) status with the IRS. Under Resolution R-23-145, an agency may not be affiliated with an abortion service provider as defined in Florida law.
programs.application: Four application types on the county's page, each with budget forms: Results First, Results First New Program, Results as Service (only for the programs the page lists) and System Advocate. Information session December 4, 2026, 10 a.m., Lakewood Ranch Library.
programs.award: Award amounts are not stated. Funded programs run October 1 to September 30.
programs.contact: Manatee County Children's Services staff, listed on the county's page
programs.subjects: Children; Youth; Families; Child welfare; Prevention; Early childhood

programs.title: Health and Human Services Investments
programs.agency: Manatee County, Community and Veterans Services Department
programs.objectives: Funding for community services that improve the health, safety, stability and quality of life of Manatee County residents. Health priorities: dental care and access to care for indigent residents, emergency sheltering, mental and behavioral health services, co-occurring disorders, and care navigators or community health workers. Human services priorities: healthy aging, disability inclusion, food security and nutrition, criminal justice reentry, affordable housing and homelessness prevention, and career development and employment.
programs.who: Agencies serving Manatee County residents that have 501(c)(3) status with the IRS and comply with Resolution R-23-145 on affiliations.
programs.application: One application type per agency: Results First (new or returning applicants) or Results as a Service (agencies already funded under that model). Application materials are posted on the county's page when the period opens. Information session December 4, 2026, 10:30 to 11:30 a.m., Lakewood Ranch Library, in person only.
programs.award: Award amounts are not stated. County staff score applications with input from the Health and Human Services Investment Review Committee, and the Board of County Commissioners decides. Funding starts October 1, 2027.
programs.contact: Manatee County Community and Veterans Services staff, listed on the county's page
programs.subjects: Health; Mental health; Disabilities; Food security; Housing; Homelessness; Employment; Aging; Reentry

programs.title: Community Event Funding
programs.agency: Juvenile Welfare Board of Pinellas County
programs.objectives: Small awards for one-time education and community resource events for children and families, local conferences on children and families, and community distribution of school supplies, emergency supplies, food or other basic needs in Pinellas County. Not for fundraising events, events held more than once a year, school-sponsored events, sports leagues, salaries, administrative costs or capital costs.
programs.who: Organizations registered as a 501(c)(3), or government entities, whose activity benefits Pinellas County children and families and fits the Juvenile Welfare Board's strategic goals. One award per fiscal year (October 1 to September 30).
programs.application: Send a signed letter on the organization's letterhead 60 to 180 days before the event, describing the activity, its budget, other funding and the amount requested, with a completed W-9, to the address in the application packet.
programs.award: $500 to $3,000. Awards are approved by the Juvenile Welfare Board's Chief Executive Officer or designee.
programs.deadlines: Rolling: the request must arrive 60 to 180 days before the event.
programs.subjects: Children; Families; Community events; School supplies; Basic needs; Education

programs.title: Cultural Development Grants
programs.agency: Arts Council of Hillsborough County (Hillsborough County)
programs.objectives: General program support for local cultural organizations whose programs serve diverse audiences in different parts of the county. The program aims to build both cultural and administrative operations and help groups reach new audiences and other funding. Disciplines include architecture, crafts, creative writing, dance, history, literature, media arts, music, photography, theatre, traditional arts and visual arts.
programs.who: Organizations whose primary mission is delivering cultural programs. Earlier guidelines required a Florida 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a principal address in Hillsborough County and excluded municipalities, government agencies, educational institutions and fiscal agents. Confirm in the FY28 guidelines.
programs.application: Online application from the Arts Council's organizational grants page, which also posts the guidelines, a sample application, the administration manual and the scoring rubric. Funded groups must show the Hillsborough County logo and a funding credit.
programs.award: Up to $25,000 in general program support.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; History; Music; Theatre; Dance; Visual arts; Literature

programs.title: Community Arts Impact Grants
programs.agency: Arts Council of Hillsborough County (Hillsborough County)
programs.objectives: Grants for arts programs that reach underserved populations in Hillsborough County. The program is also meant as a first step for small organizations that are new to grant writing.
programs.who: Nonprofit organizations offering arts programs in Hillsborough County. See the current guidelines for the full rules.
programs.application: Online application from the Arts Council's organizational grants page. Funded groups must show the Hillsborough County logo and a funding credit.
programs.award: Up to $5,000 for nonprofit organizations.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; Underserved communities; Capacity building

programs.title: Special Event Partnership Grants
programs.agency: Arts Council of Hillsborough County (Hillsborough County)
programs.objectives: Support for cultural special events in Hillsborough County. Fundraising events are not eligible.
programs.who: Organizations producing cultural special events in Hillsborough County. See the current guidelines for eligibility.
programs.application: Online application from the Arts Council's organizational grants page. Funded groups must show the Hillsborough County logo and a funding credit.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; Events; Festivals; Tourism

programs.title: Historic Preservation Challenge Grant
programs.agency: Hillsborough County
programs.objectives: County grants for projects that preserve historic resources in Hillsborough County.
programs.who: Nonprofit organizations or private parties with a historic preservation project in Hillsborough County. Government agencies are not eligible.
programs.application: Apply through the county's program page, which posts the guidelines and form for each cycle.
programs.award: Amount varies; see the current guidelines.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The 2026 deadline was May 1, 2026; the 2027 date is not posted yet.
programs.subjects: Historic preservation; History; Architecture; Community development

programs.title: Opioid Settlement Fund Request for Applications
programs.agency: Hillsborough County
programs.objectives: Hillsborough County awards its share of Florida opioid settlement money to programs that address opioid use disorder through prevention, treatment and recovery.
programs.who: Organizations serving Hillsborough County residents. See each RFA for eligibility.
programs.application: Submissions go through e2Hillsborough when a cycle is open. Email the county to get notice of the next RFA.
programs.award: Set in each RFA.
programs.deadlines: The 2025 RFA has closed. The county expects the next cycle in late 2026 or early 2027.
programs.subjects: Substance use; Opioids; Behavioral health; Prevention; Treatment; Recovery

programs.title: Emerging Needs Grant
programs.agency: Children's Board of Hillsborough County (Children's Services Council)
programs.objectives: One-time funding for community needs that could not be foreseen when the Children's Board adopted its yearly budget. The need must fit the board's focus areas, such as children being healthy and safe and developmentally on track. Board policy limits funded work to 18 months.
programs.who: Nonprofit or government organizations legally operating in Florida that serve Hillsborough County children and families. Board documents focus on pregnant women and children from birth to age 8 and their families; a later webinar described children from birth to 18.
programs.application: Read the Emerging Needs information on the Children's Board funding opportunities page and contact staff before applying.
programs.deadlines: Considered during the fiscal year as needs arise, while funds last.
programs.subjects: Children; Families; Early childhood; Maternal health; Child safety

programs.title: CDBG Public Services Request for Applications
programs.agency: City of Tampa
programs.objectives: Federal Community Development Block Grant money the City of Tampa awards to public service programs for low- and moderate-income Tampa residents.
programs.who: Nonprofit organizations running public service programs that meet HUD CDBG rules and serve Tampa residents.
programs.application: Yearly RFA with a technical assistance workshop, a question period, a compliance review and an evaluation committee.
programs.award: Set in each year's RFA.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The FY27 (program year 2026) RFA closed April 30, 2026; watch for the next RFA in early 2027.
programs.subjects: Community development; Low income; Public services; Human services

programs.title: TPD C.A.R.E.S. Grants
programs.agency: City of Tampa, Tampa Police Department
programs.objectives: Community grants from the Tampa Police Department for local organizations' programs in Tampa. See the program page for the current focus.
programs.who: Community organizations serving Tampa. See the program page for eligibility.
programs.application: Apply from the program page during an open cycle.
programs.deadlines: See the program page for the current cycle.
programs.subjects: Public safety; Youth; Community; Neighborhoods

programs.title: Alcohol and Drug Abuse Trust Fund
programs.agency: Pinellas County Human Services
programs.objectives: One-time special projects for substance use services in Pinellas County, such as equipment, training, renovations and prevention. Food and drink costs are not allowed. The Substance and Alcohol Abuse Advisory Board recommends awards and the Board of County Commissioners approves them.
programs.who: 501(c)(3) nonprofits incorporated in Florida for at least one year, licensed under Chapter 397, Florida Statutes, with a service location in Pinellas County.
programs.application: Apply through Neighborly from the Pinellas County Human Services site (www.pinellascounty.org/humanservices). Funded projects run October 1 to September 30.
programs.award: $35,000 available in total; awards of $1,000 to $10,000.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The FY27 window was May 20 to June 17, 2026 at 2 p.m.; expect the next one in spring 2027.
programs.subjects: Substance use; Behavioral health; Prevention; Equipment; Training

programs.title: Arts Tourism Funding Program
programs.agency: Creative Pinellas for Pinellas County, funded by Visit St. Pete-Clearwater
programs.objectives: Competitive awards for arts experiences that draw visitors to Pinellas County during a month-long arts celebration (Art Everywhere). The County Commission approved $500,000 for the first year in March 2026.
programs.who: Arts and culture nonprofits, for-profit arts organizations and individual artists creating arts experiences in Pinellas County.
programs.application: Online application through Creative Pinellas during an open cycle.
programs.award: Organizations $15,000 to $50,000; individual artists $5,000 to $15,000.
programs.deadlines: The first cycle closed May 31, 2026, and about $350,000 was awarded. A next cycle depends on county tourism funding.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; Tourism; Events

programs.title: City of the Arts Grant
programs.agency: City of St. Petersburg
programs.objectives: City grants for arts and culture nonprofits whose programs take place in St. Petersburg.
programs.who: Nonprofit arts and culture organizations with yearly budgets over $50,001, located in St. Petersburg, with more than half of their programming in the city.
programs.application: Online application and guidelines on the city's arts grants page.
programs.award: Several funding levels; see the current guidelines.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The 2026 cycle opened April 2, 2026; the 2025 cycle closed June 13.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture

programs.title: Level Up Arts Grant
programs.agency: City of St. Petersburg
programs.objectives: Small city grants for St. Petersburg's smaller arts nonprofits.
programs.who: Nonprofit arts organizations with yearly budgets of $50,000 or less. See the program page for location rules.
programs.application: Online application from the program page.
programs.deadlines: The 2026 round was open until April 30, 2026 or until funds ran out.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; Small organizations; Capacity building

programs.title: Social Action Funding
programs.agency: City of St. Petersburg
programs.objectives: City funding for programs that serve people experiencing homelessness in St. Petersburg.
programs.who: Nonprofits providing homelessness services in St. Petersburg. See the guidelines.
programs.application: Apply from the program page during an open cycle.
programs.award: Earlier cycles awarded up to $50,000.
programs.deadlines: The 2026 cycle opened May 4, 2026. See the page for the next cycle.
programs.subjects: Homelessness; Housing; Human services

programs.title: MLK Grant
programs.agency: City of St. Petersburg
programs.objectives: City mini-grants tied to the Martin Luther King Jr. observance in St. Petersburg. See the program page for what is funded.
programs.who: Community organizations in St. Petersburg. See the program page for eligibility.
programs.application: Apply from the program page during an open cycle.
programs.award: Mini-grants; see the program page for amounts.
programs.deadlines: Yearly, ahead of Martin Luther King Jr. Day. See the program page for dates.
programs.subjects: Community; Civic engagement; Events; Culture

programs.title: Youth Opportunity Grants
programs.agency: City of St. Petersburg
programs.objectives: City grants for youth programs in St. Petersburg. See the program page for the current focus.
programs.who: Organizations running youth programs in St. Petersburg. See the program page for eligibility.
programs.application: Apply from the program page during an open cycle.
programs.award: See the program page for amounts.
programs.deadlines: See the program page for the current cycle.
programs.subjects: Youth; Education; Out-of-school time

programs.title: Cultural Affairs Nonprofit Grant Program
programs.agency: City of Clearwater
programs.objectives: City grants for cultural programs and projects that benefit Clearwater.
programs.who: Public entities or Florida nonprofit, tax-exempt corporations. Groups do not have to be based in Clearwater, but the benefit must be local.
programs.application: Apply separately for each unique cultural program or project. A sample application is posted.
programs.award: Varies by project; no organization may receive more than $250,000 in total over the program.
programs.deadlines: See the city's site for the current cycle.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; Events

programs.title: Public Service Provider Funding (CDBG)
programs.agency: City of Clearwater, Affordable Housing and Community Development
programs.objectives: Federal CDBG funding for public service programs serving low- and moderate-income Clearwater residents, set through the city's Annual Action Plan.
programs.who: Nonprofit public service providers serving Clearwater residents.
programs.application: Yearly application tied to the Annual Action Plan.
programs.award: Set each year in the Annual Action Plan.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. Applications start in January or February and the cycle ends when City Council approves the Annual Action Plan.
programs.subjects: Community development; Low income; Public services; Housing

programs.title: CDBG, HOME and ESG Grant Applications
programs.agency: Manatee County, Community and Veterans Services Department
programs.objectives: Federal HUD funds (Community Development Block Grant, HOME and Emergency Solutions Grant) for housing, public services and community development serving low- and moderate-income residents and people experiencing homelessness in Manatee County.
programs.who: Nonprofit agencies serving Manatee County residents, plus county departments.
programs.application: Attend the yearly Grant Application Workshop, then apply during the application period. A selection committee reviews and the Board of County Commissioners votes.
programs.award: About $2.5 million in total each year. ESG for 2026-27 was about $160,000 for street outreach, shelter, prevention, rapid re-housing and HMIS.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The program year 2026 window was March 2 to 31, 2026; expect the next window in March 2027.
programs.contact: Julia Vieira, Community Development Project Manager
programs.subjects: Housing; Homelessness; Community development; Low income; Public services

programs.title: SHIP Homebuyer Education Funding
programs.agency: Manatee County, Community and Veterans Services Department
programs.objectives: State Housing Initiatives Partnership money for approved nonprofit housing counseling agencies that give homebuyer education to Manatee County residents.
programs.who: Nonprofit housing counseling agencies approved by Manatee County.
programs.application: Contact the Community and Veterans Services Department for the application.
programs.deadlines: Nonprofit applications opened April 15, 2026, with funds available until committed.
programs.subjects: Housing; Homeownership; Financial education

programs.title: Contracted Human Services
programs.agency: Sarasota County Health and Human Services
programs.objectives: About $25 million a year in county contracts with nonprofits for human services and behavioral health. The Behavioral Health and Human Services Advisory Councils review applications.
programs.who: Nonprofit agencies serving Sarasota County residents.
programs.application: Apply each year through e-CImpact.
programs.award: Set per contract; about $25 million in total each year.
programs.deadlines: Yearly cycle; see the county page for dates.
programs.subjects: Human services; Behavioral health; Mental health; Substance use; Families

programs.title: Tourist Development Cultural/Arts Program
programs.agency: Arts and Cultural Alliance of Sarasota County, for Sarasota County
programs.objectives: Fee-for-service funding from the county's tourist development tax for performances, exhibitions and events that draw visitors to Sarasota County. Projects are judged on tourist appeal, artistic or cultural purpose and administrative ability.
programs.who: Arts and cultural organizations with at least one year of stable arts or cultural programming.
programs.application: The Alliance issues a request for proposals and a panel reviews applications. The Tourist Development Council recommends awards and the County Commission approves them. Contracts for 2027 added new terms tied to a state law, so read the current terms before applying.
programs.award: Varies by project; about $2.1 million in total for FY2026.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. Applications are usually due in spring, with county approval in July.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; Tourism; Events

programs.title: Opioid Treatment, Prevention and Recovery Fund
programs.agency: Pasco County Opioid Task Force
programs.objectives: Opioid settlement grants for evidence-based treatment, prevention and recovery from substance use disorders in Pasco County.
programs.who: Community-based organizations serving Pasco County.
programs.application: Attend a virtual information session to get the application link. The task force recommends awards and the Board of County Commissioners approves them.
programs.award: Varies; earlier rounds awarded more than $8 million across projects.
programs.deadlines: The Year Four window (June 10 to July 10, 2026) was paused on May 20, 2026 while the community reviews a USF gap analysis. New dates are pending.
programs.subjects: Substance use; Opioids; Behavioral health; Prevention; Treatment; Recovery

programs.title: CDBG and ESG Public and Homeless Services RFA
programs.agency: Polk County Housing and Neighborhood Development
programs.objectives: Federal CDBG and ESG funds for public services and homeless services in Polk County. Priority needs have included serving people with disabilities, preventing child abuse or neglect, serving homeless people and assisting victims.
programs.who: Nonprofit organizations serving Polk County.
programs.application: Yearly RFA submitted through Neighborly Software, with a technical assistance workshop.
programs.award: Set in each RFA.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The 2026-27 portal was open February 24 to March 24, 2026; expect the next RFA in February 2027.
programs.subjects: Homelessness; Human services; Disability; Child abuse prevention; Victim services

programs.title: Public Service Grants (CDBG)
programs.agency: City of Lakeland, Community and Economic Development
programs.objectives: The City of Lakeland gives about $160,000 a year to nonprofit public service programs serving low- and moderate-income clients, in categories such as child care.
programs.who: Nonprofit public service agencies and local government programs serving low- and moderate-income Lakeland clients. Public school programs are not eligible.
programs.application: Online application. This is a reimbursement grant: the agency pays program costs first and the city repays them.
programs.award: About $160,000 in total each year.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The 2026-2027 deadline was March 27, 2026.
programs.subjects: Human services; Child care; Low income; Public services

programs.title: Mayor's Council on the Arts Grant
programs.agency: City of Lakeland, Mayor's Council on the Arts
programs.objectives: General program support for arts organizations carrying out their mission in Lakeland.
programs.who: Arts organizations. To ask for more than $25,000, a group needs at least 3 years of programming and at least one paid full-time manager.
programs.application: Read the yearly guidelines, then apply online from the City Clerk's page. A panel of council members who did not apply scores and ranks applications.
programs.award: Varies; awards are reduced proportionally when requests exceed the money available.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The 2026-2027 deadline was September 15, 2026.
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture

programs.title: Neighborhood Partnership Matching Grant
programs.agency: City of Lakeland
programs.objectives: Matching grants for neighborhood projects: physical improvements and beautification, better association operations, crime reduction, youth program costs and resource conservation.
programs.who: Lakeland neighborhood associations with at least one strong project partner. The association must endorse the application.
programs.application: Submit a complete application by the deadline, following the yearly guidelines.
programs.award: Matching grant; see the guidelines for amounts.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. 2026/27 applications were due in August 2026.
programs.subjects: Neighborhoods; Beautification; Public safety; Youth; Conservation

programs.title: Grant Aid
programs.agency: City of Winter Haven
programs.objectives: City grant aid for nonprofit organizations serving Winter Haven.
programs.who: Nonprofits serving Winter Haven. Applicants must complete the required training.
programs.application: Complete the required training, then apply during the yearly window.
programs.award: See the city page for amounts.
programs.deadlines: Yearly. The current fiscal year window was March 2 to 13, 2026.
programs.subjects: Community; Human services
